newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway's UBN books lower Q1 profits.
newsitem.headline: Norway's UBN books lower Q1 profits.

text.p: Union Bank of Norway, Norway's largest savings bank, on Tuesday recorded an operating profit after losses of 360 million crowns ($50.8 million), a drop of about 10 percent from the corresponding period last year.
The bank, known locally as Sparebanken NOR, attributed the lower result to a 50 million crown loss on a guarantee in respect of NOKA Securities, a recently defuncted Oslo brokerhouse.

But the operating profit before losses was 385 million crowns, an improvement of 23 million crowns. The profit after tax was 264 million, down from 298 million and representing a return on equity of almost 17 per cent.

"This is a very good result for the bank," Kjell Kran, the group's President and Chief Executive Officer, said in a statement. "Over the last two and a half years, UBN's quarterly results have fluctuated between approximately 300 million crowns and 400 million. Earnings are therefore stable and high." ($ = 7.093 Norwegian Crowns)
